config.title: Build an image carousel with autoplay and pause

intro.title: Build an image carousel with autoplay and pause
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build an interactive image carousel that automatically cycles through a set of pictures and allows the user to pause the slideshow. You'll learn how to use JavaScript's `setInterval` and `clearInterval` functions to control timed events, which is the core programming concept for implementing autoplay and pause functionality. The main technologies involved are HTML for the image structure, CSS for basic styling, and vanilla JavaScript for the dynamic behavior. By the end, you'll have a working carousel that demonstrates fundamental DOM manipulation and timer management in a practical project.
intro.usecase: Image carousels with autoplay are ubiquitous in modern web interfaces, appearing in e-commerce product galleries, news website featured content sections, and portfolio showcases. Developers implement this pattern in dashboards to cycle through key metrics, in marketing sites to highlight promotions, and in media platforms to display photo albums. The autoplay functionality keeps content engaging while the pause control gives users agency to examine items at their own pace. Mastering this component helps you build professional interfaces that balance automated presentation with user control.

objectives: Construct an image carousel component with a dynamic array of image sources
Initialize and manage state variables for the current image index and autoplay status
Implement navigation handlers to control the previous and next image display
Configure an autoplay interval that automatically cycles through images
Integrate pause and resume controls to manipulate the autoplay functionality
Render visual indicators to display the current position within the image set
Update the displayed image based on user interactions and autoplay events

steps.title: Import React and useState
steps.instruction: Import React and the useState hook from the 'react' package.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in React and useState from 'react'.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: importing React and a hook
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have the necessary imports to start building your carousel component with state management.
successCriteria: React and useState are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're importing both React and useState from 'react'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check the import statement. You need to import React and useState from 'react'.

steps.title: Create the Carousel component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named Carousel that returns an empty div element.
steps.hint: Define the component using either a function declaration or arrow function syntax. Make sure it returns a div.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState } from 'react';

// Create the Carousel component here
steps.expectedOutcome: A Carousel component is defined and returns an empty div.
successCriteria: The Carousel component is defined and returns a div element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the Carousel component structure.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the component is named Carousel and returns a div.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component isn't defined correctly. Check that you've named it Carousel and it returns a div.

steps.title: Initialize image array state
steps.instruction: Inside your Carousel component, initialize a state variable named 'images' using useState. Set its initial value to an array containing at least three image URLs (e.g., 'image1.jpg', 'image2.jpg', 'image3.jpg').
steps.hint: Use the useState hook you imported earlier. The syntax is: const [images, setImages] = useState([...]). Provide an array of strings as the initial state.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: initializing an array state
const [items, setItems] = useState(['apple', 'banana', 'orange']);
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a state variable 'images' storing an array of image URLs, ready to be used for the carousel slides.
successCriteria: The state variable 'images' is declared with useState, and its initial value is an array of at least three image URL strings.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started the state initialization, but make sure 'images' is declared with useState and its initial value is an array of image URLs (strings).
steps.feedbackWrong: The images state isn't properly initialized. Use useState to create a state variable named 'images' with an array of image URLs as the initial value.

steps.title: Initialize current image index state
steps.instruction: Inside the Carousel component, initialize a state variable named 'currentIndex' with a default value of 0 using useState.
steps.hint: Add a new useState call after your images state. Remember to destructure useState from React.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: initializing state for a counter
const [count, setCount] = useState(0);
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now has a state variable 'currentIndex' that tracks which image is currently displayed, starting with the first image (index 0).
successCriteria: A state variable 'currentIndex' is declared using useState with an initial value of 0.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using useState to create a state variable named 'currentIndex' with an initial value of 0.
steps.feedbackWrong: Inside the Carousel component, use useState to create a state variable called 'currentIndex' that starts at 0.

steps.title: Initialize autoplay state
steps.instruction: Inside your Carousel component, add a new state variable called 'isPlaying' with a default value of true using useState.
steps.hint: Add another useState call after your currentIndex state. Remember to destructure isPlaying and setIsPlaying from useState.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: initializing a boolean state
const [isActive, setIsActive] = useState(true);
steps.expectedOutcome: Your component will have a third state variable to track whether autoplay is active.
successCriteria: A state variable 'isPlaying' is declared with useState, initialized to true, and placed after the currentIndex state.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using useState to declare 'isPlaying' with a default value of true.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't match what we need. Look at the hint and try adding the autoplay state variable.

steps.title: Create next image handler
steps.instruction: Inside your Carousel component, create a function named 'goToNext' that updates the currentIndex state to show the next image, wrapping back to 0 when reaching the end of the images array.
steps.hint: You can use setCurrentIndex to update the state. Calculate the next index as (currentIndex + 1) % images.length to handle wrapping.
steps.expectedOutcome: A function named goToNext is defined that correctly calculates and sets the next image index with wrap-around behavior.
successCriteria: The goToNext function is defined, uses setCurrentIndex, and correctly implements (currentIndex + 1) % images.length logic.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started the function, but make sure it correctly calculates the next index with wrap-around using the modulo operator.
steps.feedbackWrong: The goToNext function isn't properly defined yet. Remember to create a function that updates currentIndex to the next image index.

steps.title: Create toggle autoplay handler
steps.instruction: Create a function named 'toggleAutoplay' that toggles the isPlaying state between true and false.
steps.hint: Use the setter function from the useState hook to update the state based on its previous value.
steps.expectedOutcome: The toggleAutoplay function is defined and uses setIsPlaying to toggle the boolean state.
successCriteria: A function named toggleAutoplay is created that toggles the isPlaying state.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your function is named 'toggleAutoplay' and uses setIsPlaying to toggle the state value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The toggleAutoplay function isn't quite right. Create a function that toggles the isPlaying state between true and false.

steps.title: Add main image display
steps.instruction: In the return statement of your Carousel component, add an img element that displays the current image from the images array using the currentIndex state.
steps.hint: Use the src attribute to set the image URL. You can access the current image with images[currentIndex].
steps.expectedOutcome: The main image display will be added to the component's return statement, showing the current image based on the currentIndex state.
successCriteria: An img element is added inside the return statement with src={images[currentIndex]} to display the current image.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the img element uses src={images[currentIndex]} to display the correct image based on the currentIndex state.
steps.feedbackWrong: The main image display wasn't added correctly. You need to add an img element with src={images[currentIndex]} inside the return statement.

steps.title: Add previous and next buttons with click handlers
steps.instruction: Inside the return statement of your Carousel component, add two button elements: one labeled 'Previous' and one labeled 'Next'. Wire the 'Previous' button's onClick to the prevImage handler and the 'Next' button's onClick to the nextImage handler.
steps.hint: Place the buttons inside the div. Use the onClick prop on each button to call the appropriate handler function.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will now have two navigation buttons that allow manual control of the carousel.
successCriteria: Two button elements exist with labels 'Previous' and 'Next'. The 'Previous' button's onClick calls prevImage and the 'Next' button's onClick calls nextImage.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added buttons, but check that each button's onClick is correctly wired to the corresponding handler function.
steps.feedbackWrong: The buttons or their click handlers are missing or incorrect. Make sure you have both 'Previous' and 'Next' buttons with onClick props calling prevImage and nextImage respectively.

steps.title: Add autoplay toggle button with click handler
steps.instruction: Inside the component's return statement, add a button element that displays 'Pause' when autoplay is active (isPlaying is true) and 'Play' when autoplay is inactive (isPlaying is false). Wire its onClick handler to toggleAutoplay.
steps.hint: Use a ternary operator to conditionally set the button text based on the isPlaying state. The button should call toggleAutoplay when clicked.
steps.expectedOutcome: A button appears in the carousel that toggles between 'Play' and 'Pause' labels based on the autoplay state and triggers the toggle handler when clicked.
successCriteria: The button element is present with onClick={toggleAutoplay} and uses a ternary to display 'Pause' when isPlaying is true and 'Play' when false.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a button, but check that the text changes based on isPlaying and the onClick is correctly set to toggleAutoplay.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button is missing or not correctly implemented. Ensure you add a button with conditional text and an onClick handler that calls toggleAutoplay.

steps.title: Implement autoplay with setInterval
steps.instruction: Add a useEffect hook that sets up an interval to automatically advance images when autoplay is active, and clears it when autoplay is inactive or the component unmounts.
steps.hint: Import useEffect from 'react', then use it inside your component. The effect should run when isPlaying changes. When isPlaying is true, set an interval that calls nextImage every 3000 milliseconds. Return a cleanup function that clears the interval.
steps.expectedOutcome: The carousel will automatically advance to the next image every 3 seconds when autoplay is active, and stop when autoplay is toggled off.
successCriteria: The useEffect hook is imported and used, with a dependency array containing isPlaying. An interval is set when isPlaying is true, calling nextImage every 3000ms. A cleanup function clears the interval.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your useEffect has the correct dependencies and includes both the interval setup and cleanup.
steps.feedbackWrong: The autoplay functionality isn't working correctly. Check that you've imported useEffect, set up the interval properly, and included a cleanup function.
